paragraphs: Friend, here's what this passage teaches me: a rule can sound strong and still do damage. Saul's oath looked serious, but the men were in distress, and Jonathan said, "My father has brought trouble to the land." (1 Samuel 14:24, 29) Then the faint troops rushed to the plunder and ate meat with the blood still in it, which the report to Saul called sinning against the LORD (1 Samuel 14:32-33). I think Saul wanted to look serious more than he wanted to look at the people in front of him.

Now look at who Saul is willing to hurt. He swore that whoever sinned must die, even Jonathan, and when the lot fell on his son, he said it again (1 Samuel 14:39, 44). Meanwhile, God did not answer him that day (1 Samuel 14:37). I'm not going to guess why, because the text doesn't say, but I will say this, friend: it's possible to be LOUD about God and still not be listening to Him.

So here's what I want you to carry out of my bakery. Don't ask only, "Am I following the rule?" Ask, "Am I listening to the LORD?" The priest said, "We must consult God here," and that's the kind of voice worth hearing (1 Samuel 14:36). And Saul's story isn't finished yet, so stay tuned.
